$comment: Strict cutover between revisions (VERSIONING.md, aitp/0.2 -> aitp/0.3). The envelope is env-007's with `version` set to the previous revision `aitp/0.2` and a fresh message_id, signed by kat-keypair-001 over sig_input_v2 = "aitp-envelope-v2" || 0x00 || JCS(envelope without `signature`). The signature is committed and valid for these exact bytes (re-signed by scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py, verified by scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs), so the only reason to reject is the revision literal. Unlike env-010, whose signature does not cover its altered `version`, nothing here is tampered: an aitp/0.3 receiver has no dual-accept window and rejects a well-signed aitp/0.2 envelope with UNKNOWN_VERSION.
description: A correctly signed envelope from the previous revision (`version` = `aitp/0.2`). aitp/0.3 is a strict cutover: a receiver implementing aitp/0.3 does not implement aitp/0.2, and RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 checks `version` first. Expected: UNKNOWN_VERSION, not success and not INVALID_SIGNATURE.

expected.rationale: `version` is `aitp/0.2`, the frozen previous revision. An aitp/0.3 receiver does not accept it (strict cutover, no dual-accept window) and the RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 check order rejects an unknown `version` with UNKNOWN_VERSION before the member set or the signature is examined. The signature itself is valid over sig_input_v2 of these bytes.
